_comment: design-gate allowlist -- accepted, already-reviewed skill routing collisions found by unmassk-toolkit/bin/design_gate.py. An entry here excludes that ONE specific finding from failing the gate (exit code), but design_gate.py still PRINTS it in every report, tagged '[allowlisted]' instead of '[NEW]' -- nothing is ever hidden. A finding not listed here is tagged '[NEW]' and fails the gate.
_how_to_add_an_exception: 1) Run `python3 unmassk-toolkit/bin/design_gate.py --json`. 2) Find the new finding and build its key: keyword_collisions -> the 'term' string; phrase_collisions -> the 'phrase' string; dangling_references -> '{skill}::{token}'; mutual_contradictions -> '{skill_a}::{skill_b}::{comma-joined sorted shared_terms}'. 3) After a human reviews the finding (confirms the overlap is expected/acceptable, not a routing bug), append the key to the matching array below. Never blanket-allow a whole category -- allowlist exact findings only.

_reasons._comment: Human-readable justification per allowlisted finding, keyed the same way as _finding_key() in design_gate.py. Purely informational -- design_gate.py's load_allowlist() only reads the 4 category arrays below by name and ignores any other top-level key, so this block is invisible to the parser/gate logic; it exists for the next human (or Alexandria) who re-reviews an entry, so nothing gets re-approved 'green by decree'.

keyword_collisions.actuator: unmassk-electronics (the core, cross-branch skill) lists 'actuator' only in its own trigger keyword list so a generic actuator request still routes into the plugin; electronics-robotics is the branch that actually owns actuator control (PCA9685/L298N/TB6612/DRV8825 patterns). Parent-skill/child-branch relationship, not two siblings claiming the same ground.
keyword_collisions.ccpa: compliance-gdpr scans CODE for CCPA-relevant PII handling (hardcoded personal data, retention checks); compliance-legal-docs drafts/reviews CCPA-relevant legal DOCUMENTS (privacy notices, DPAs). Same regulation, different artifact (code scan vs document drafting) -- same split as the gdpr entry below.
keyword_collisions.connection pooling: db-postgres covers Postgres-specific pooling (PgBouncer, process-architecture model); db-redis covers Redis client-side pooling/multiplexing (redis-py, Jedis, Lettuce). Same generic infra term, two different databases with different pooling mechanics.
keyword_collisions.data breach: compliance-legal-docs owns the legal DOCUMENT side of a breach (the GDPR 72h notification letter, breach-sentinel .docx templates); compliance-soc2-iso owns the security INCIDENT-RESPONSE playbook side (SEV-1/2 triage, ransomware response). Drafting the notification vs running the IR process -- distinct domains.
keyword_collisions.dpa: compliance-gdpr's reference covers DPA (Art. 28) as one item in a code-level GDPR posture scan; compliance-legal-docs is where an actual DPA (data processing agreement) document gets reviewed/drafted. Same code-scan-vs-document-drafting split as ccpa/gdpr.
keyword_collisions.gdpr: Three distinct lenses on the same regulation, verified against each skill's own reference table: compliance-gdpr = code-level scanning (PII detection, ROPA/DPIA/breach-notification posture check against a codebase); compliance-legal-docs = legal document drafting/review (privacy notices, DPAs, breach letters); compliance-soc2-iso = security-program/framework building (GDPR as one program alongside SOC2/ISO27001/HIPAA, timelines and control mapping). No two of the three do the same job.
keyword_collisions.hipaa: compliance-gdpr scans code for HIPAA-relevant PII/PHI handling as part of its multi-regulation PII detector; compliance-soc2-iso builds the HIPAA compliance PROGRAM (Covered Entity/BAA scoping, notification timelines, security-control roadmap alongside SOC2/ISO27001). Code scan vs org-level framework building.
keyword_collisions.hreflang: compliance-i18n mentions hreflang as one of the locale-routing concepts an i18n implementation must get right (next-intl, RTL); unmassk-seo owns the actual hreflang AUDIT (8-check validation, international SEO scoring). Implementation-support mention vs the skill that owns validating it.
keyword_collisions.mrr: Same 3-letter acronym, two unrelated meanings, confirmed in each skill's own text: db-vector-rag's MRR is Mean Reciprocal Rank (a retrieval-quality metric, next to NDCG/Recall@K); unmassk-marketing's MRR is Monthly Recurring Revenue (next to ARR/CAC/LTV/churn). A homonym collision, not a domain overlap -- the linter can't tell acronyms apart by string alone.
keyword_collisions.pgvector: Already documented as an explicit, deliberate boundary inside both skills themselves (db-postgres: 'db-vector-rag: RAG pipeline architecture beyond the pgvector extension itself'; db-vector-rag: 'db-postgres: PostgreSQL-specific operations beyond pgvector (MVCC, VACUUM, partitioning)') -- db-postgres owns the extension/ops side, db-vector-rag owns the RAG-pipeline/embedding side built on top of it.

phrase_collisions.onboarding flow: unmassk-design's ux-writing reference covers onboarding COPY (microcopy, button labels, voice/tone for the flow's screens); unmassk-marketing's retention reference covers onboarding flow STRATEGY (churn prevention, lifecycle stage, paywall timing). Writing the words vs designing the strategy around them.

mutual_contradictions.design-motion::design-taste::slop: A heuristic blind spot, not a real gap: both design-motion and design-taste correctly defer generic 'AI slop' critique to the core skill, and design-taste's own SKILL.md says so explicitly ('unmassk-design (the core skill) already owns the generic anti-slop checklist -- the AI Slop Test'). The core's frontmatter mentions the AI Slop Test only in body prose, never in its structured 'mentions any of:' keyword list, so the linter's word-overlap check (which only reads mention_terms/quoted_phrases) can't see that the ground IS claimed. Confirmed by grepping 'slop' across all 3 files directly, not from memory.
